title: Ya-Sin 36:65-67 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 37 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ya-Sin 36:65-67 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 37. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَتَشْهَدُ أَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ (٦٥) وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَطَمَسْنَا عَلَىٰٓ أَعْيُنِهِمْ فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَٰطَ فَأَنَّىٰ يُبْصِرُونَ (٦٦) وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَمَسَخْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِهِمْ فَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ مُضِيًّۭا وَلَا يَرْجِعُونَ (٦٧)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: That Day, We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn.
And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to [find] the path, and how could they see?
And if We willed, We could have deformed them, [paralyzing them] in their places so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.

questions.q: Chunk and link Ya-Sin 36:65-67 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 36:65-67 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 36:65-67 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
Allah could take away their sight or transform them; they live by His mercy and should not be ungrateful.

questions.q: Link 36:65 to how we use phones and keyboards.
questions.a: Our hands will speak about what we typed and shared: use them for good.

questions.q: What will testify on that Day (36:65)?
Ya-Sin 36:65: «ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: On that Day mouths are sealed and hands and feet speak (36:65). How might that change how you use your hands and feet today?
questions.a: Use them only for good: they will testify about what we did.
